data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Manual (DM) provides procedures to accompany Departmental Regulation (DR) 3465-001, Enterprise Geospatial Data Management.
cross_references: Departmental Regulation (DR) 3465-001, Enterprise Geospatial Data Management

policy_statements.source_text: This DM enhances data sharing and reuse throughout the data lifecycle for discovery, access, and interoperability with machine-readable, searchable standard metadata using the Federal Geographic Data Committee (FGDC)-Endorsed Metadata Standards, per the FGDC Geospatial Standards web page.
This DM supports DR 3465-001.

It applies to all United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, programs, teams, organizations, appointees, and employees, including contractors and grantees receiving Federal funds that utilize and collect geospatial data.
policy_statements.target: United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, programs, teams, organizations, appointees, and employees, including contractors and grantees receiving Federal funds that utilize and collect geospatial data
conditions: that utilize and collect geospatial data

policy_statements.source_text: Use this DM along with DR 3465-001.
This DM is effective immediately when published.
conditions: when published

policy_statements.source_text: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will align processes, procedures, and application of metadata standards with this DM for geospatial authoritative data (GAD) within 6 months of publication.
policy_statements.actor_name: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: processes, procedures, and application of metadata standards
conditions: for geospatial authoritative data (GAD)
within 6 months of publication

policy_statements.source_text: This section describes how a FGDC-Endorsed Metadata Standard is interpreted for USDA-funded geospatial metadata to increase its value for both USDA and other geospatial data creators and users.
Establishment of the USDA geospatial metadata standard:
The metadata standard adopted by USDA must meet the following criteria.
The metadata standard must be endorsed and recommended by the FGDC; and
The implementation must fully support the metadata standard.
Every metadata element and attribute defined in the metadata standard must be available for the creation, maintenance, import, and export of metadata.
policy_statements.target: Every metadata element and attribute defined in the metadata standard

policy_statements.source_text: This requirement ensures that no metadata content is lost during the transfer of a record between systems fully supporting the metadata standard.
The preferred FGDC-Endorsed Metadata Standard is the USDA representation of geospatial metadata, serving as the authoritative version of the metadata, if a derived or exported format differs.
conditions: if a derived or exported format differs

policy_statements.source_text: USDA-Specific Metadata:
USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices may add requirements for metadata elements.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will use this DM as their internal policy.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: They may create a more restrictive policy, but they will not create a policy that is less restrictive or less comprehensive than, or not compliant with, this DM.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: that is less restrictive or less comprehensive than, or not compliant with, this DM

policy_statements.source_text: USDA metadata must adhere to FGDC-Endorsed Metadata Standards, regardless of the tools used to create, maintain, manage, or use metadata.
conditions: regardless of the tools used to create, maintain, manage, or use metadata

policy_statements.source_text: Allowable changes to the official metadata standard will include, but are not limited to:
Requiring metadata that is optional in the metadata standard; and
policy_statements.target: metadata that is optional in the metadata standard

policy_statements.source_text: Requiring the use of specific lists of values to use for particular elements.
policy_statements.target: use of specific lists of values to use for particular elements

policy_statements.source_text: Well-known and widely used lists are preferable to creating a new list.
USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices may define quality requirements for the content of elements to improve Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable (FAIR) characteristics;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: quality requirements for the content of elements

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices may enforce additional interrelationships between elements and element values;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: additional interrelationships between elements and element values

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices may require metadata at various stages of the geospatial data lifecycle; and
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: at various stages of the geospatial data lifecycle

policy_statements.source_text: Categories or types of geospatial data may have different metadata requirements from other geospatial data.
policy_statements.target: Categories or types of geospatial data

policy_statements.source_text: All geospatial metadata must be valid.
For geospatial metadata, valid means that:
The metadata contains the required metadata elements;
The format meets the structure and content defined by FGDC-Endorsed Metadata Standards;
policy_statements.target: structure and content defined by FGDC-Endorsed Metadata Standards

policy_statements.source_text: Interrelationships between elements specified in the metadata standard are enforced; and
policy_statements.target: Interrelationships between elements specified in the metadata standard

policy_statements.source_text: The metadata from USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must meet the applicable criteria identified in Section 4c(4).
Metadata Workflows:
Geospatial data creators must minimize duplicate submission of metadata to geospatial catalogs, geospatial portals, and other collections and inventories, and must choose one of the following:
FGDC GeoPlatform.gov;
General Services Administration (GSA) Data.gov; or
Any USDA data catalog identified by the Office of the Chief Information Officer’s (OCIO) Enterprise Geospatial Management Office (EGMO).
Geospatial data creators may be required to output FGDC-endorsed metadata in various other formats to facilitate intersystem services and readability.
policy_statements.target: FGDC-endorsed metadata in various other formats

policy_statements.source_text: Metadata Access:
Metadata must be available when data is downloaded, obtained from a web service, or otherwise distributed.
conditions: when data is downloaded, obtained from a web service, or otherwise distributed

policy_statements.source_text: Metadata must be available in an FGDC-Endorsed Metadata Standard format.
For metadata standards-based geospatial data formats that permit the inclusion of metadata with the data, the metadata must be included.
conditions: For metadata standards-based geospatial data formats that permit the inclusion of metadata with the data

policy_statements.source_text: For download formats that do not embed metadata, the link for the data download is to be accompanied by an equally prominent link to download the metadata in the required FGDC-Endorsed Metadata Standard.
conditions: For download formats that do not embed metadata

policy_statements.source_text: Additional links to metadata in other formats are acceptable only if the required metadata standard is also available.
policy_statements.target: Additional links to metadata in other formats
conditions: only if the required metadata standard is also available

policy_statements.source_text: If metadata (and data) are available using web services, open standard services must be used even if proprietary services are also implemented.
conditions: If metadata (and data) are available using web services
even if proprietary services are also implemented

policy_statements.source_text: Metadata must be downloadable in FGDC-Endorsed Metadata Standard formats from the geospatial catalogs.
Geospatial metadata must accompany geospatial data during the Federal records management processes identified in DR 3080-001, Records Management.
conditions: during the Federal records management processes identified in DR 3080-001, Records Management

policy_statements.source_text: Common metadata-derived products may be identified as required or optional.
Potential purposes may include but are not limited to:
Web page content for optimizing search engine indexing of data; and
Alternative display formats for metadata viewed on a web page.
Metadata Creation and Curation:
Valid metadata is needed for GAD.
The OCIO EGMO Geospatial Information Officer (GIO) may authorize and allow use of certain data before comprehensive metadata is finalized.
conditions: before comprehensive metadata is finalized

policy_statements.source_text: Valid metadata must meet USDA requirements before their release.
conditions: before their release

policy_statements.source_text: Metadata must be included with the data when retention of the data is required.
conditions: when retention of the data is required

policy_statements.source_text: This includes litigation holds, Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) (5 United States Code (U.S.C.), § 552, Public information; agency rules, opinions, orders, records, and proceedings) requests, or other administrative or legal mandates.
cross_references: Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) (5 United States Code (U.S.C.), § 552, Public information; agency rules, opinions, orders, records, and proceedings)

policy_statements.source_text: This may require retention of data and metadata for specific versions or revisions of the data or products.
conditions: for specific versions or revisions of the data or products

policy_statements.source_text: Updates to published metadata must be documented within the metadata record to inform geospatial data creators and users of the change.
Due diligence must be used when moving metadata records to ensure that links to related metadata within the control of the Department, Mission Area, agency, or staff office remain valid.
conditions: when moving metadata records

policy_statements.source_text: Curation may be required for the development and maintenance of shared, reusable metadata building blocks and other approaches to reduce metadata creation effort and improve consistency with shared metadata building blocks.
Acquired Geospatial Data:
Geospatial data paid for in whole or in part from other sources must comply with FGDC-Endorsed Metadata Standards.
policy_statements.target: Geospatial data paid for in whole or in part from other sources

policy_statements.source_text: USDA-funded data includes contracts to acquire data, purchase of existing data, cooperative agreements, grants, cost sharing, and other means of procurement.
Address metadata requirements with respect to:
Variations in the funding source and acquisition vehicle;
USDA funding a portion of the acquisition costs;
The type and urgency of data;
Allocation of metadata creation between the provider and acquiring entity;
Use of no-cost data that is not accompanied by FGDC-Endorsed Metadata Standards; and
Other significant characteristics.

Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will use Geospatial Data Act (GDA) (codified at 43 U.S.C. Ch. 46, Geospatial Data) instructions for new contracts and agreements for new metadata requirements.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: Geospatial Data Act (GDA) (codified at 43 U.S.C. Ch. 46, Geospatial Data) instructions
conditions: for new contracts and agreements for new metadata requirements
cross_references: Geospatial Data Act (GDA) (codified at 43 U.S.C. Ch. 46, Geospatial Data)

policy_statements.source_text: The roles and responsibilities identified in this DM align to DR 3465-001.
The USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO) will:
Delegate executive leadership for geospatial technology, data, and information solutions to the USDA GIO;
policy_statements.target: executive leadership for geospatial technology, data, and information solutions

policy_statements.source_text: Approve revisions; and
Review and approve processes, procedures, and metadata standards for waiver or exception requests.
policy_statements.target: processes, procedures, and metadata standards for waiver or exception requests

policy_statements.source_text: As the owner of this DM, the CIO will have the final review and approval authority for any waiver or exception requests.
The USDA GIO will:

Serve as the senior executive responsible for Departmental geospatial strategy, planning, coordination, assessment, and synchronization of all USDA geospatial data activities assigned to the GIO per Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular A-16, Revised, Coordination of Geographic Information and Related Spatial Data Activities, requirements;
cross_references: Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular A-16, Revised, Coordination of Geographic Information and Related Spatial Data Activities
policy_statements.target: Departmental geospatial strategy, planning, coordination, assessment, and synchronization of all USDA geospatial data activities assigned to the GIO

policy_statements.source_text: Have authority, responsibility, and coordination for USDA’s geospatial information technology (IT) portfolio;

Oversee and facilitate USDA internal and external implementation of the geospatial IT and geospatial data policies, governance, directives, requirements, management, product, and service standardization;
policy_statements.target: USDA internal and external implementation of the geospatial IT and geospatial data policies, governance, directives, requirements, management, product, and service standardization

policy_statements.source_text: Review geospatial procedural DMs.
Ensure that they provide specific guidance.
The CIO will approve these prior to publication;
conditions: prior to publication

policy_statements.source_text: Serve as the policy-level official representing USDA at the FGDC;
policy_statements.resulting_status: policy-level official representing USDA at the FGDC

policy_statements.source_text: Appoint Mission Area, agency, and staff office representatives to serve on FGDC coordination groups, governance, and working groups;
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office representatives

policy_statements.source_text: Maintain a knowledge base of USDA geospatial portfolio investments;
policy_statements.target: knowledge base of USDA geospatial portfolio investments

policy_statements.source_text: Oversee the enterprise geospatial capital planning process per DR 3130-013, Information Technology Capital Planning and Investment Control; and
cross_references: DR 3130-013, Information Technology Capital Planning and Investment Control

policy_statements.source_text: Oversee the enterprise geospatial investment control process per DR 3130-010, United States Department of Agriculture Enterprise Information Technology Governance; and advocate for Mission Area, agency, and staff office geospatial portfolio budgets and acquisition plans;
cross_references: DR 3130-010, United States Department of Agriculture Enterprise Information Technology Governance

policy_statements.source_text: Advocate for the use, value, and benefits of geospatial innovation and information supporting decision makers, citizens, partners, and others;
policy_statements.target: use, value, and benefits of geospatial innovation and information supporting decision makers, citizens, partners, and others

policy_statements.source_text: Collaborate with the CIO, EGMO Program Manager (PM), the USDA Chief Data Officer, and other OCIO Service Center Associate CIOs (ACIO) to implement strategic initiatives;
policy_statements.target: CIO, EGMO Program Manager (PM), the USDA Chief Data Officer, and other OCIO Service Center Associate CIOs (ACIO)

policy_statements.source_text: Provide the Departmental response to external geospatial portfolio data calls; and
policy_statements.target: Departmental response to external geospatial portfolio data calls

policy_statements.source_text: Review and provide a recommendation to the CIO on any submitted and completed waivers to the primary requesting office for any requirement that is not in compliance with this DM.
conditions: for any requirement that is not in compliance with this DM

policy_statements.source_text: The CIO, as the policy owner, will make the final decision.
The EGMO PM will:
Initiate reviews and updates to this DM in a timely manner;
policy_statements.target: reviews and updates to this DM
conditions: in a timely manner

policy_statements.source_text: Act as the primary Departmental PM for geospatial matters, overseeing and coordinating various programs, projects, and staff;
Support and coordinate the geospatial portfolio with USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices; and

Collaborate with USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices researching new geospatial technologies and potential implementations across Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices to meet geospatial data management requirements.
policy_statements.target: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices researching new geospatial technologies and potential implementations across Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA Chief Data Officer will collaborate with the CIO, the GIO, the EGMO PM, and OCIO Service Center ACIOs on geospatial matters to implement strategic initiatives.
policy_statements.target: CIO, the GIO, the EGMO PM, and OCIO Service Center ACIOs

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office Geospatial Leads will:
Use FGDC-Endorsed Geospatial Data Standards per the GDA, and as stated on the FGDC Geospatial Standards web page;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office Geospatial Leads

policy_statements.source_text: For all geospatial data, follow USDA-specific requirements for metadata content, to include future DMs and guidelines;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office Geospatial Leads
conditions: For all geospatial data

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that metadata is certified and documented:
The specific Mission Area, agency, or staff office owner will certify all metadata as compliant with data standards;
policy_statements.actor_name: specific Mission Area, agency, or staff office owner

policy_statements.source_text: Metadata will include identification that confirms its nature as authoritative data;
policy_statements.target: identification that confirms its nature as authoritative data

policy_statements.source_text: Metadata will be documented in an authoritative system that can be queried to find the data themes in OMB Circular A-16; and
All metadata will be certified and documented even if the underlying data is subject to restrictions on public release;
conditions: even if the underlying data is subject to restrictions on public release

policy_statements.source_text: Make the metadata available through the FGDC’s GeoPlatform, unless legally restricted;

extract_result.purpose:
a. This Departmental Manual (DM) provides procedures to accompany Departmental Regulation (DR) 3465-001, Enterprise Geospatial Data Management.
b. This DM enhances data sharing and reuse throughout the data lifecycle for discovery, access, and interoperability with machine-readable, searchable standard metadata using the Federal Geographic Data Committee (FGDC)-Endorsed Metadata Standards, per the FGDC Geospatial Standards web page.
extract_result.scope: This DM supports DR 3465-001. It applies to all United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, programs, teams, organizations, appointees, and employees, including contractors and grantees receiving Federal funds that utilize and collect geospatial data.

a. This Departmental Manual (DM) provides procedures to accompany  Departmental Regulation (DR) 3465-001 , *Enterprise Geospatial Data Management*.

b. This DM enhances data sharing and reuse throughout the data lifecycle for discovery, access, and interoperability with machine-readable, searchable standard metadata using the Federal Geographic Data Committee (FGDC)-Endorsed Metadata Standards, per the  *FGDC Geospatial Standards*  web page.

It applies to all United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, programs, teams, organizations, appointees, and employees, including contractors and grantees receiving Federal funds that utilize and collect geospatial data.

This section describes how a FGDC-Endorsed Metadata Standard is interpreted for USDA-funded geospatial metadata to increase its value for both USDA and other geospatial data creators and users.
Establishment of the USDA geospatial metadata standard:
The metadata standard adopted by USDA must meet the following criteria.
The metadata standard must be endorsed and recommended by the FGDC; and
The implementation must fully support the metadata standard.
Every metadata element and attribute defined in the metadata standard must be available for the creation, maintenance, import, and export of metadata.
Every metadata element and attribute defined in the metadata standard
This requirement ensures that no metadata content is lost during the transfer of a record between systems fully supporting the metadata standard.
The preferred FGDC-Endorsed Metadata Standard is the USDA representation of geospatial metadata, serving as the authoritative version of the metadata, if a derived or exported format differs.
if a derived or exported format differs

This DM supports DR 3465-001. It applies to all United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, programs, teams, organizations, appointees, and employees, including contractors and grantees receiving Federal funds that utilize and collect geospatial data.
